players.note: Will Anderson was back at it in Week 5, reeling off three solos, one assist, three sacks, and three tackles for loss. Anderson has been on fire for the Texans, recording three splash weeks and one spike week in five games. The Texans edge rusher leads the league with 7.5 sacks, recording at least a half sack in every contest this season. Fire him up as the number one at the position until further notice.

Arvell Reese was at it again in Week 5, racking up three solos, six assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Reese has now registered two splash weeks followed by a spike week, vaulting him to LB3 overall on the season. Tap Arvell as a top-10 option as long as he is cooking.

Danielle Hunter showed up in Week 5, notching three solos, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Hunter has just two spike weeks ot his name but has recorded at least a half sack in four straight games. He is up to a solid enough three sacks on the season and remains a top-12 option due to his propensity to get sacks in bunches. Treat him as such for a plus Week 6 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

DeForest Buckner was back at it in Week 5, registering three solos, four assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Buckner now has three spike weeks to his name and is up to 3.5 sacks on the season. Count DeForest as an easy DT1 who doubles as a DL2/DL3 play for Week 6 and beyond.

David Bailey showed out in Week 5, racking up five solos, two assists, three sacks, and three tackles for loss. Bailey is now up to five sacks on the season, with at least one sack in three of the first five games of his career. The DL3 in total fantasy points after the splash week, Bailey can now be counted as a top-15 option going forward.

Josh Hines-Allen showed up in Week 4, tallying four solos and two tackles for loss. Hines-Allen has not recorded a sack since Week 1 and still sits at 1.5 sacks for the season. Treat the Jaguars edge rusher as a DL2/Dl3 type until he starts to get rolling.

Abdul Carter stepped up in Week 5, tallying two solos, three assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. It was just the second sack of the season for Carter, who is facing more double teams with Brian Burns lost for the season. This was supposed to be a breakout season for the Giants pass rusher, and while he remains a pressure machine, they have not been translating to sacks. Count Carter as more DL2 than DL1 until he starts to heat up for the Giants, but don't put him on your bench. Carter is an elite talent who should start to get sacks in bunches. Tap Carter as a top-25 option for a plus Week 6 matchup against the New Orleans Saints. Start Carter everywhere.

Zach Allen was at it again in Week 5, generating one solo, two assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. One of the most underrated front seven defenders in the league due to technically being an interior offensive lineman, Allen is up to four sacks on the season with at least one sack in three of his five games played. It was the second spike week for Allen who remains an elite DL3/DT1 play. The DL14 through five weeks of play needs to be started everywhere.

Leonard Williams has been excellent this season, starting the campaign with a sack in three tsriaight games. His production has taken a hit since suffering an ankle injury in Week 4, but looks to have turned a corner as the Seahawks did not list him with an injury status for Thursday Night Footall. Fire Williams up as DT1/DL2 option despite the tough on paper matchup.

Nik Bonitto was at it again in Week 5, tallying three solos, one assist, two sacks, and three tackles for loss. Bonitto is up to three sacks on the season, with all three coming in his last three games. Bonitto is one of the best in the league when he is on, and his recent production suggests that he is ready to roll. Tap him as a top-10 option for a plus Week 6 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.

Austin Booker was excellent in Week 5, racking up four solos, one assist, two sacks, three tackles for loss, and one forced fumble. Booker is up to four sacks on the season, with at least one sack in three of his last four games. Tap Booker as a top-25 option for Week 6, thanks both to his hot streak and a plus matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

Jalen Carter went off in Week 5, exploding with three solos, two assists, two sacks, three tackles for loss, two forced fumbles, and one pass defended. Carter is now up to three sacks on the season and reminded fantasy managers of why you need to start him even during valleys; you don't want to miss a peak. Tap Carter as a DT1/DL3 for a plus Week 6 matchup against the Carolina Panthers.

Elijah Ponder was at it again in Week 5, racking up four solos, two assists, two sacks, two tackles for loss, and one forced fumble. Ponder is up to a new career high of 4.5 sacks and should have at least a few more weeks of starter-level snaps while Harold Landry remains on the mend. Ponder has a tasty matchup in Week 5 against the New York Jets, making him a DL2 option. Tap Ponder as a top-25 option as long as he is cooking.

Tavius Robinson showed out in Week 5, racking up three solos, three assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and one pass defended. Tavius is up to three sacks on the season, with at least one sack in three of his five games. The DL22 through five weeks of action, Robinson should be counted as an elite DL3 option for Week 6, thanks to a tasty matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

Carl Granderson showed up in Week 5, racking up two solos, three assists, 1.5 sacks, and two tackles for loss. Granderson is up to 2.5 sacks on the season and is a solid DL3 during the byes, including this week, thanks to a plus Week 6 matchup against the New York Giants.

Byron Murphy was at it again in Week 5, racking up five solos, one assist, two sacks, and three tackles for loss. Murphy is up to three sacks on the season, with all three coming in his last two games. His hot streak puts him in the DT1 mix for the byes and makes him a deep league DL3 option during the byes. However, Murphy should remain on fantasy benches for Thursday Night Football. Look elsewhere for Week 6.

Will McDonald showed up in Week 5, racking up one solo, three assists, one sack, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery. It was the second sack of the season for McDonald, who has been a massive disappointment in 2026. David Bailey was always expected to dominate snaps on one side, but ceding snaps to the more effective Kinsley Enagbare was not in the cards for those who drafted or added McDonald this season. Tap him as a DL3 option during the byes, but be cognizant of his waiver wire floor.

Akheem Mesidor stepped up in Week 5, tallying five solos, three assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Mesidor is up to 2.5 sacks on the season, with a sack in two of his last three games. Akheem has looked the part through the first five weeks of the season and may be set to see an expanded role in the near future with Khalil Mack emerging as one of the hottest trade candidates in the league. Mesidor should be rostered in all leagues as a bye week depth piece who could emerge as a DL2/3 option in the next couple of weeks.

K'Lavon Chaisson showed up in Week 5, reeling off one solo, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Chaisson has zero spike weeks but is up to a solid 2.5 sacks on the season, with at least a half sack in three of his last four games. K'Lavon can be counted as a top-36 option for a plus Week 6 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

Daron Payne was excellent in Week 5, tallying one solo, two assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. It was the first sack of the season for Payne, who remains on the Dt2 periphery due to his slow start. Feel free to ignore him in DL leagues until he shows some more fantasy production.

Devonte Wyatt showed up in Week 5, recording three solos, two assists, two sacks, two tackles for loss, and one forced fumble. The sacks were the first of the season for Wyatt, who remains more DT2 than DT1 until he shows some consistency. Feel free to ignore Wyatt in all but the deepest DL leagues until that happens. Look elsewhere for Week 6.

Mike Green was excellent in Week 5, racking up two solos, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Green is up to two sacks on the season and makes for a solid DL3 option for Week 6, thanks to a tasty matchup against the Cleveland Browns. Start the Ravens pass rusher where needed.

Princely Umanmielen was at it again in Week 4, racking up three solos, one sack, and one tackle for loss on a season high 52 percent of the snaps. Princely has been a force off the edge for the Panthers, recording a sack in three of his first four contests of the season. He could see an expanded role in Week 6 if Jaelan Phillips sees his snaps scaled back in an effort to prevent further injury. If Jaelan Phillips misses Week 6, Umanmielen becomes a must-start DL3 with DL2 upside.

Maliek Collins stepped up in Week 5, registering two solos, two assists, 1.5 sacks, and two tackles for loss. Collins is up to 2.5 sacks on the season and has recorded back-to-back spike weeks. His recent production pushes him into the DT1 conversation and gives him DL3 upside for Week 6, thanks to a date with a shaky Baltimore Ravens offensive line. Start Collins where needed.

Keion White was excellent in Week 5, racking up three solos, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Keion is now up to three sacks on the season and has recorded at least one sack in three of his last four games. White has seen an expanded role over the last two weeks due to Nick Bosa being sidelined with a quad injury and has produced well enough to factor prominently in the rotation until he cools down.

Gracen Halton had the game of his career in Week 5, tallying three solos, one sack, two tackles for loss, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery, and one touchdown. It was a massive splash week for Halton, but it was his first sack of the season. The DL16, due to the explosion of fantasy points, Halton should be left on the bench until he shows more consistency. Look elsewhere for Week 6.

Dani Dennis-Sutton stepped up in Week 5, tallying three solos, one sack, and two tackles for loss. DDS is up to 1.5 sacks on the season and is playing enough to be a deep league option during the byes. With Micah Parsons not yet ready to return for Week 6, Sutton becomes a DL3/4 option for a plus matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

Roy Lopez showed up in Week 5, racking up three solos, three assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss on 55 percent of the snaps. It was the first sack of the season for Lopez, who failed to record a pressure all season before the meeting with the Lions. Lopez now belongs on 32 team radars but should not yet even be a DT3 consideration in 12 team leagues. Add him to watchlists, but look elsewhere for Week 6.

Baron Browning showed up in Week 5, tallying two solos, two assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and two forced fumbles on 43 percent of the snaps. It was the first sack of the season for Browning, who is more of a deep league bench option than someone those in 12 team leagues should have on their radars, at least for now.

Baron Browning showed up in Week 5, tallying two solos, two assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and two forced fumbles on 43 percent of the snaps. It was the first sack of the season for Browning, who is more of a deep league bench option than someone those in 12 team leagues should have on their radars, at least for now.

D.J. Jones showed up in Week 5, tallying one solo, three assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss on 46 percent of the snaps. The sack was the first of the season for Jones, who is part of a deep rotation along the Broncos' defensive interior. Keep him in mind for 32-team leagues but look elsewhere for Week 6 in all other formats.
